intro: Buying a home in Nevada involves more than comparing purchase prices and mortgage rates. Property taxes, homeowners insurance, association fees and recurring household expenses can significantly affect how much you need to budget each month.

Our free Nevada mortgage calculator estimates your monthly housing payment using your home price, down payment, interest rate and repayment period. Whether you're purchasing in Las Vegas, Henderson, Reno, Carson City or another Nevada community, use the calculator to compare financing options before making an offer.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Nevada?

blocks.markdown:
A $435,000 Nevada home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed annual interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $2,086.44.

An illustrative monthly housing payment breakdown is shown below.
This example assumes no private mortgage insurance. Interest rates, taxes, insurance premiums and association fees are illustrative rather than current statewide averages.

Nevada offers housing opportunities across metropolitan neighborhoods, master-planned communities, mountain towns and rural areas.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Nevada QuickFacts](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/NV/POP060220), the median value of owner-occupied housing was $435,400 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among households with mortgages were $1,932, while approximately 60% of occupied housing units were owner-occupied.

These historical figures provide useful context but do not represent current property asking prices. Existing homeowners may have purchased their properties years earlier at different interest rates and prices.

Housing expenses in southern Nevada can differ considerably from those in northern Nevada. Properties near Reno and Lake Tahoe may also present different insurance and maintenance considerations.

Research comparable property sales within your preferred neighborhood before establishing your purchase budget.

sections.heading: How to Use the Nevada Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Enter the expected purchase price of your property and the amount you intend to contribute as a down payment.

Select your preferred repayment period and enter the annual interest rate quoted by your lender.

If you have not received a quote, consult [Freddie Mac's mortgage market survey](https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms) for a national reference.

Next, include annual property taxes, homeowners insurance premiums and monthly association fees.

Add private mortgage insurance if your conventional financing requires it.

Review the estimated monthly housing payment and experiment with different purchase prices, loan terms and down payments.

The amortization schedule shows how your remaining mortgage balance changes over time and how much interest you could pay.

Use our national Mortgage Calculator to compare financing arrangements outside Nevada.

sections.heading: How Nevada Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
Nevada calculates property taxes using a system involving taxable property values, assessed values, local tax district rates and applicable abatements.

Understanding these distinctions can help you avoid overestimating or underestimating your future property tax liability.

### Nevada taxable and assessed property values

According to the [Clark County Assessor's real property guidance](https://www.clarkcountynv.gov/government/assessor/real-property), taxable value generally combines the market value of the land with the replacement cost of improvements, adjusted for statutory depreciation.

The assessor's taxable value may therefore differ from the property's purchase price.

Nevada then applies a statutory assessment ratio of 35% to taxable value.

For example, if a property's taxable value is $350,000, its assessed value would be $122,500.

Applicable tax district rates are applied to this assessed amount.

### Nevada property tax calculation example

Suppose you purchase a home for $435,000, and the county assessor establishes a taxable value of $350,000.

Assume a hypothetical combined tax rate of $3 per $100 of assessed value.

The property's actual tax liability may be lower because of applicable abatements.

Consult the [Washoe County Assessor's valuation guidance](https://www.washoecounty.gov/assessor/real_property/UnderstandingYourValueNotice.php) or your relevant county assessor for property-specific information.

### Nevada's 3% property tax cap

Nevada provides a partial property tax abatement for qualifying owner-occupied primary residences. This generally limits eligible annual property tax increases to 3%, subject to statutory exceptions.

The restriction concerns the amount of tax payable, not annual increases in property market value or the underlying tax rate.

For example, if a qualifying property's previous annual tax bill was $2,700, a fully applicable 3% limitation would generally produce a maximum of $2,781 for the covered tax liability the following year.

New construction, classification changes and other statutory circumstances can affect the calculation.

The [Washoe County Assessor's tax cap explanation](https://www.washoecounty.gov/assessor/faq/TC_Is_MyTax_Rate_Capped.php) provides additional clarification.

Confirm the property's abatement classification and any required declarations before using the previous owner's tax bill as your estimate.

Homeowners insurance premiums depend on the property's location, construction, condition, rebuilding cost and environmental exposure.

The [Nevada Division of Insurance's homeowners insurance guide](https://doi.nv.gov/Consumers/Homeowners_Insurance/Homeowners__Insurance/) explains how these factors influence premiums and coverage.

Obtain property-specific quotes before finalizing your purchase.

### Wildfire insurance considerations

Properties near forests, grasslands and mountainous areas may face additional wildfire exposure.

Ask insurers whether your property's location affects coverage availability, premiums or required mitigation measures.

Investigate the condition of roofing materials, surrounding vegetation and emergency access.

Do not assume that every homeowners insurance provider will offer identical coverage for a high-risk property.

### Flood and earthquake insurance

Nevada's dry climate does not eliminate flood risk. Heavy rainfall, snowmelt and changing drainage conditions can produce flooding.

The [Nevada Division of Insurance's flood insurance guidance](https://doi.nv.gov/Flood-Insurance/) explains that ordinary homeowners insurance excludes flood damage.

Standard policies also generally exclude earthquakes.

Use the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home) to investigate the property's flood exposure.

Include any additional insurance premiums in your annual mortgage estimate without counting overlapping coverage twice.
The following estimates assume a 20% down payment, a 6% fixed annual interest rate and a 30-year mortgage.

These estimates exclude property taxes, homeowners insurance, mortgage insurance and association fees.

The Nevada Housing Division offers mortgage financing and purchase assistance through participating lenders.

### Home Is Possible for First-Time Homebuyers

The [Home Is Possible First-Time Homebuyer program](https://www.homeispossiblenv.org/home-possible-program) provides eligible buyers with down payment and closing cost assistance of up to 4% of their qualifying mortgage amount.

The assistance is structured as an interest-free, non-forgivable second mortgage with a 30-year term.

Applicants generally must not have owned a home during the previous three years. Credit score, income, property eligibility and homebuyer education requirements also apply.

### Home Is Possible for repeat buyers

The standard [Home Is Possible program](https://www.homeispossiblenv.org/home-possible) offers assistance of up to 5% of the qualifying mortgage amount.

Applicants do not necessarily need to be first-time homebuyers.

The published program requirements include qualifying income of up to $165,000 and a maximum purchase price of $832,750, subject to loan-specific restrictions.

For example, 5% assistance on an eligible $348,000 first mortgage would amount to $17,400.

This financing can reduce upfront cash requirements but should not be treated as an unconditional grant.

Compare assistance-based financing with ordinary mortgage offers and confirm repayment requirements with an approved lender.

sections.heading: HOA Fees and Additional Homeownership Costs in Nevada

blocks.markdown:
Buyers considering master-planned communities or condominiums should investigate recurring association fees before purchasing.

Some properties may have both neighborhood association dues and master association fees.

Request the complete fee schedule, review reserve funds and investigate potential special assessments.

Southern Nevada homeowners should also account for summer cooling expenses, water consumption, landscaping and swimming pool maintenance.

Properties in northern Nevada may require additional winter heating, snow removal and weather-related maintenance.

These expenses are not automatically included in the calculator's mortgage estimate. Add them separately when establishing your broader household budget.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Nevada?

blocks.markdown:
Begin with reliable monthly take-home income and subtract existing financial obligations.

Nevada does not impose an individual state income tax, but federal income taxes and applicable payroll deductions still reduce take-home earnings.

Our [Nevada Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/nevada-paycheck-calculator/) can help estimate after-tax income, while our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) can help evaluate existing borrowing commitments.

Allow sufficient room for insurance deductibles, utilities, transportation, groceries and emergency savings.

Compare mortgage offers using the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/).

Choose a property whose complete housing expenses remain manageable alongside your other financial priorities.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $435,000 Nevada home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, monthly principal and interest would be approximately $2,086.44. Property taxes, homeowners insurance and applicable fees increase the total housing payment.

### Does Nevada limit property tax increases to 3%?

Qualifying owner-occupied primary residences generally benefit from a 3% annual property tax abatement limitation. Statutory exceptions apply, and the limitation is not a universal property tax rate.

### Does Nevada offer down payment assistance?

Yes. The Nevada Housing Division's Home Is Possible programs provide qualifying borrowers with assistance of up to 4% or 5% of their mortgage amount, depending on the selected program. Eligibility and repayment requirements apply.
